From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@healthsync.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Ephemeral session policy & privileged account artifacts request

Vanessa —

Thanks for the time on the call earlier. As part of our SIG/SOC2 evidence intake we need to collect a short package related to privileged access and ephemeral sessions for Redwood-hosted accounts that access PHI environments. Can you provide the following artifacts by EOD Tuesday (3 business days)?

- Owner roster for privileged accounts (CSV with username, role, owner, last activity)
- SCIM delta logs covering Nov 10–12 (we only need deltas showing adds/removes for service accounts)
- A runbook or short write-up describing ephemeral session enforcement (token TTLs, JIT elevation, approval flow)
- One redacted SAML assertion sample for a user promoted to a privileged role (timestamps and Subject / NameID OK; please redact PII)

If you need a longer timeline, let me know. Also specify any constraints on sharing (e.g., attachments via shared Drive link only).

Appreciate it — we’re trying to close this control set for our auditor.

— Alice
Alice Moreno
Director, Security Assurance | HealthSync
alice.moreno@healthsync.com

Alice —

Thanks — we can get that to you. Quick plan: I’ll own the privileged owner roster, Michael will export the SCIM delta logs and a SAML assertion sample (redacted), and Jonas will draft a 1–2 page runbook outlining TTLs and JIT controls. We may need to share the raw SCIM JSON via a Drive link for size reasons.

Couple clarifying Qs before we package:
- Do you want the owner CSV to include service account keys metadata (last key rotation date) or just account owners and last activity?
- For the SAML sample: redaction OK for NameID and email, but do you need the full Assertion with Conditions (timestamps) preserved?

I’ll target an initial artifact drop Monday EOD PT with final files Tuesday morning if that works for you.

Thanks,

From: michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference>

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Ephemeral session policy & privileged account artifacts request — artifacts attached

Vanessa / Alice —

Attaching the artifacts requested. See notes below and attachment stubs: privileged-owners.csv, scim-delta-snapshot-20261112.json, ephemeral-session-runbook.pdf. Because the SCIM delta JSON is large we placed the full export in Drive and attached a trimmed snapshot here. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_epi-session-evidence

Notes:
- Privileged accounts roster (privileged-owners.csv): contains account id, role label (admin, infra-operator, db-admin), primary owner (manager on record), last-login timestamp (UTC). Service account keys summary (rotation date) included for accounts with keys.
- SCIM deltas: our provisioning sync runs nightly at 02:00 UTC. The attached snapshot includes add/remove events (Nov 10–12) for service accounts and role assignments. Full retention of SCIM deltas is 90 days in our audit storage.
- Ephemeral sessions: token TTLs are 1 hour by default. JIT elevation for privileged actions is mediated through our internal access service (AccessGate). Elevations require an approval from an owner for sessions >30 minutes or for elevations that involve production write scopes. Audit trail is stored in our immutable event log; retention 365 days. Details in ephemeral-session-runbook.pdf.
- SAML assertion sample: included as a redacted block in the Drive folder (saml-assertion-sample-redacted.xml) — we removed NameID/email and replaced with <REDACTED>. Conditions and timestamps intact. If you need a signed raw assertion we can provide it under an SCP.

Attachments (stubs):
- privileged-owners.csv (CSV, 42 rows)
- scim-delta-snapshot-20261112.json (JSON, trimmed snapshot)
- ephemeral-session-runbook.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

Michael / Vanessa —

Received the Drive link and the attached snapshots — thank you. A quick follow-up: can you export one exported SAML assertion sample for a user who was elevated to a privileged role (redacted as you described) and include the X509 Subject name for the signing cert (we only need the cert DN, not the cert material)? That will satisfy our assertion validation step.

If you can drop that into the same Drive folder and reply here, we’ll mark this control as 'evidence provided' and pass to the auditor.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alice
